q.t: Can we see energy itself?
o: No — we only see what it does
q.e: We see things move, shine, sound, warm or cool — the signs of energy.

q.t: A plucked rubber band makes sound because it…
q.e: Sound needs vibration — moving rapidly to and fro.

q.t: What is the fuel for our bodies?
q.e: Every movement is paid for out of what we eat.

q.t: In an oil lamp, what is the fuel?
q.e: The wick only carries oil up to the flame.

q.t: Most electricity in India is made by burning…
q.e: Coal power makes lots of smoke and harmful gases.

q.t: Which is a clean energy source?
q.e: Sun, wind and flowing water give energy without smoke.

q.t: The main source of energy for life on Earth is…
q.e: Follow almost any energy chain back and you reach the Sun.

q.t: An LED bulb compared to an old bulb…
o: Gives the same light using less electricity
q.e: That is energy efficiency — same work, less energy.

q.t: Why do torches and phones need batteries?
o: To store energy for when no supply is attached
q.e: Batteries keep energy until it's needed.

q.t: What should you do if you see a fallen electric wire?
o: Stay away and tell an adult
q.e: A live wire looks exactly like a dead one, so never touch.

q.t: A balloon flies forward when air rushes out backwards because…
o: The air pushes back on the balloon as it leaves
q.e: Everything that pushes gets pushed back — that's how rockets work.

q.t: A dry wick burns out in seconds; an oiled wick burns long. Why?
o: The oil is the real fuel
q.e: A lamp burns as long as it is fed oil.

q.t: Why do we feel tired when hungry?
o: Our fuel supply is running low
q.e: Tiredness is what running low on fuel feels like.

q.t: Why is electricity so useful?
o: It can turn into almost any other form of energy
q.e: The same wires can run a fan, iron, bulb, bell or fridge.

q.t: Why are coal and wood not 'clean'?
o: They must be burnt, which always makes smoke and ash
q.e: Burning always produces something — smoke, gases, ash.

q.t: Why are Sun and wind called renewable?
q.e: The Sun rises again; coal, once burnt, is gone forever.

q.t: Thicker or looser rubber bands give a…
q.e: They vibrate more slowly, giving a lower note.

q.t: Which uses the Sun's energy directly?
q.e: Sun-drying uses sunlight with nothing in between.

q.t: A gharaat is a…
q.e: It grinds grain using flowing water.

q.t: The tides are driven mainly by…
q.e: Tides are the chief exception to 'everything traces back to the Sun'.

q.t: A magnifying glass burns paper because it…
o: Concentrates sunlight onto a tiny spot
q.e: The same energy lands on a much smaller area. Concentrating is not creating.

q.t: Trace the energy chain: you run after eating a chapati. Where did the energy first come from?
o: The Sun, which grew the wheat
q.e: The plant grew using sunlight; follow the chain back and you reach the Sun.

q.t: Petrol's energy came originally from…
o: Sunlight captured by ancient living things
q.e: Petrol formed from very ancient living things that grew in sunlight.

q.t: The hardest part of using clean energy is…
q.e: The Sun doesn't shine at night, so better batteries matter.

q.t: Switching off a fan in an empty room is…
q.e: No comfort was being delivered to anyone.

q.t: Why do smoke-free stoves matter?
o: Smoke in a closed kitchen harms health
q.e: Cleaner fuel is a health question first.

q.t: Why does a rocket move in empty space with nothing to push against?
o: It pushes on its own exhaust
q.e: Like the balloon, it pushes gas out and is pushed the other way.

q.t: Families in Ladakh keep cattle on the ground floor because…
o: The animals' body heat warms the home above
q.e: A traditional use of energy from living bodies.

q.t: Vaastu shastra placed rooms and windows to…
o: Make best use of natural light, wind and heat
q.e: Good placement keeps homes bright and airy without electricity.

q.t: Coal is useful even though dirty because…
q.e: It sits in a heap until burnt — no storage problem.

q.t: The Sun gives the Earth in one hour more energy than…
o: All humans use in a whole year
One city uses in a day
q.e: That's how enormous the Sun's supply is.

q.t: Which shows energy as movement?
o: A balloon flying across a room
A cup warming in the sun
q.e: The balloon moves; the others show heat, sound and light.

q.t: An electric iron turns electricity into mainly…
q.e: Electricity becomes whatever the plugged-in device needs.

q.t: Bhadla Solar Park in Rajasthan is…
o: One of the world's largest solar plants
A wind farm in the sea
q.e: It captures sunlight on a huge scale.

q.t: Why are safety rules about electricity 'stay away', not 'be careful'?
q.e: You can't inspect your way to safety.

q.t: Ancient traders from Gujarat sailed to Africa using…
q.e: Sails catch wind — clean energy used for centuries.

q.t: Which change is energy efficiency?
o: Using two bulbs instead of one
q.e: Same light, less electricity.

q.t: Your brain uses energy…
q.e: It never stops working.

q.t: Which is the best reason solar power needs batteries for a village?
o: People want light at night when there's no sun
q.e: Energy must be kept until it's needed.

q.t: A solar cooker uses mirrors to…
q.e: Same principle as the magnifying glass.
